decision: 10/10 next exact pending IDs reviewed from actual bodies and callers. 5 operate in print-query/close-slip assembly, 1 is the custody warning lambda, and 4 are layout/ESC-POS formatting. reviewed_callables.callees: LoadShiftIdentityAsync; ShiftReconciliation.ComputeBreakdownAsync; Expenses AsNoTracking query/group; LoadCloseWarningsAsync; PrintRules.ComposeShiftCloseTicket.
reviewed_callables.actual_behavior: Loads shift identity/opening cash; recomputes breakdown from current rows. It takes ActualCash from persisted shift, takes ExpectedCash and CashDifference from persisted close values when present (otherwise computes fallback), overwrites those headline fields into the recomputed breakdown, groups currently paid-from-drawer expenses by category and passes warnings/reason to a pure ticket composer.
reviewed_callables.inputs_outputs_side_effects: Reads persisted shift totals and current order/refund/movement/expense rows; returns ticket. No SaveChanges or ledger write in this function.
reviewed_callables.financial_relevance: FINANCIAL_PRESENTATION: the printed breakdown/expense categories support close reconciliation. Conditional consistency concern exists only if related rows can change after close: headline totals may be frozen while explanatory breakdown is current. This pass did not establish post-close mutation policy or confirm an actual mismatch.
reviewed_callables.counterevidence: ShiftReconciliation.ComputeBreakdownAsync is also used for close/preview, so reprint matches the same calculation method. Persisted close headline values are preferred when present.
reviewed_callables.disposition: NO_CONFIRMED_DEFECT; retain conditional FIN-PRINT-CLOSE-SLIP-RECOMPUTE-001 for mutability/revision-policy review.

reviewed_callables.financial_relevance: FINANCIAL_PRESENTATION: exposes expense composition for cash-close reconciliation; does not post or adjust expenses.
reviewed_callables.disposition: NO_ACCOUNTING_MUTATION; subject to the same conditional post-close-detail consistency question as the containing slip method.

DeliveryVerticalSliceTests comments at 823-831 repeat the day-not-shift distinction. Thus all-open scope is source-consistent with stated intended handover context. DeliveryRules.UnsettledCustodyForShift filters by delivery shift, but rg found no production callers; it is exercised only by its helper test, so it does not establish this slip's scope.
reviewed_callables.test_source: DeliveryRulesTests lines 115-130 validates the separate per-shift helper; DeliveryVerticalSliceTests lines 823-860 verifies a same-shift open custody appears on the slip and stays outstanding. Neither was executed; integration case does not include a second shift.
reviewed_callables.disposition: SOURCE-INTENDED_GLOBAL_BUSINESS_DAY_WARNING; no scope defect established. Runtime and cross-shift integration behavior remain untested.

conditional_questions.question: Can order/refund/expense/movement rows contributing to the slip breakdown be changed after shift close?
conditional_questions.source_fact: Slip recomputes breakdown and expense categories from current rows but prefers persisted close headline values when present.
conditional_questions.effect_if_true: Printed current detail may fail to explain the frozen close headline even though no new accounting mutation occurs during printing.
conditional_questions.evidence_needed: Writer/mutability policy and a post-close data change/reprint test, if such mutation is supported.

conditional_questions.question: Is a global open-custody warning on a shift slip an unintended scope leak?
conditional_questions.answer: Current evidence supports intended business-day/global context: domain and integration-test comments explicitly call custody a day obligation and say it should appear on shift handover slips. The per-shift helper is not used by the production print query. No accounting effect and no defect shown.
conditional_questions.remaining_limit: No cross-shift fixture in the cited integration test; test/runtime behavior unverified.
